hints: Look carefully at what changes and what stays the same in each product, starting by listing the functional groups in compound X.
In reaction 1 only the aldehyde group becomes a carboxylic acid while the secondary alcohol and ketone are untouched, so think mild versus strong oxidising agent.
In reaction 2 both the aldehyde and ketone become alcohols, so think which reagent reduces C=O bonds but leaves the existing O-H group alone.
walkthrough:
**Identify the functional groups in X**

Compound X contains three different groups. From left to right there is a secondary alcohol, a ketone in the middle, and an aldehyde on the right.

$$\text{X = secondary alcohol + ketone + aldehyde}$$

**Analyse reaction 1**

The product still has the same $\text{-OH}$ and the same ketone $\text{C=O}$, but the terminal $\text{-CHO}$ has become $\text{-COOH}$. This is selective oxidation of an aldehyde only.

$$\text{-CHO} \rightarrow \text{-COOH}$$

**Choose the oxidising agent**

Hot acidified $\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is strong and in excess. It would oxidise the aldehyde to acid but also oxidise the secondary alcohol to a ketone, giving a diketone acid. That is not seen. Tollens reagent is mild and oxidises only aldehydes to carboxylate ions, then $\text{HCl(aq)}$ protonates to the acid, leaving alcohol and ketone unchanged. That matches perfectly.

**Analyse reaction 2 and choose the reducing agent**

The product has three $\text{-OH}$ groups and no $\text{C=O}$. The aldehyde has become a primary alcohol and the ketone has become a secondary alcohol.

$$\text{-CHO} \rightarrow \text{-CH}_2\text{OH} \quad \text{and} \quad \text{>C=O} \rightarrow \text{>CH-OH}$$
$\text{NaBH}_4$ does exactly this reduction of aldehydes and ketones. $\text{Na}$ metal does not, it just reacts with $\text{-OH}$ groups to give $\text{H}_2$ and alkoxides. So reaction 2 needs $\text{NaBH}_4$.

options.A: Hot acidified dichromate(VI) is too strong for reaction 1. It would oxidise the secondary alcohol to a ketone as well as the aldehyde to acid. Na is also wrong for reaction 2 because Na reacts with alcohols to give hydrogen and -ONa, it does not reduce aldehydes and ketones to alcohols.
options.B: Reaction 2 reagent is correct, NaBH4 does reduce both aldehyde and ketone to alcohols. But reaction 1 reagent is wrong, hot acidified dichromate(VI) in excess would also oxidise the secondary alcohol group to a second ketone, which is not observed in the product.
options.C: Reaction 1 reagent is correct, Tollens reagent followed by HCl(aq) selectively oxidises only the aldehyde to carboxylic acid. But reaction 2 reagent is wrong, Na metal will not reduce C=O bonds, it only deprotonates the O-H groups.
options.D: This matches both changes. Tollens reagent oxidises aldehydes only, leaving ketones and alcohols alone, then HCl gives the free -COOH for reaction 1. NaBH4 reduces both aldehydes to primary alcohols and ketones to secondary alcohols for reaction 2, leaving the original alcohol unchanged.
